Chapter 3: The Power of Affirmations and Positive Statements
Now that you’ve started building new beliefs and tapped into some powerful spiritual laws, let’s look at the next step—harnessing the incredible power of your own words. I’m talking about affirmations and positive statements.
Have you ever noticed how the things you say to yourself, over and over, eventually start to shape the way you think, feel, and even act? That’s no accident. When you repeat words with genuine conviction, you can actually retrain your mind—reshaping old patterns, and nudging your life in a brand-new direction.
So, what exactly are affirmations? Think of them as simple, present-tense statements about the reality you want to create. They’re like little reminders you give your subconscious, helping to gently replace old, limiting stories with ones that are far more empowering.
It’s a bit like learning a new language. At first, saying these new phrases might feel awkward or even a bit forced. But with regular practice, suddenly, they start to feel familiar—almost natural.
Here’s an example. Imagine someone who’s always believed that “money is hard to come by.” Instead, they start each day affirming, “Abundance flows to me easily and freely.” At first, this probably feels pretty far from the truth. But by repeating it every morning, every night, or anytime doubts creep in, the mind starts to open up to new possibilities. What happens next? Little by little, their self-talk shifts, and that leads to new choices—and new results.
To get the most from affirmations, here are a few tips to keep in mind:
First, always use the present tense. Speak as if what you want is already happening.
Second, make your statements positive and specific. Focus on what you want, not what you’re trying to avoid.
Third, repetition is your friend. The more consistently you use your affirmations, the more your mind starts to accept them.
And lastly, feel the emotion behind your words. Try to really believe what you’re saying, instead of just repeating it by rote.
Let me share a real-world example. There was a retiree who’d spent years feeling anxious about money. She started using affirmations like, “I am open to new sources of income.” Within just a few months, she was invited to join a part-time consulting project. Not only did it ease her worries, but it also gave her a whole new sense of purpose.
You can create affirmations for any part of your financial life—welcoming surprise income, feeling worthy of abundance, trusting that resources will flow, or letting go of fear and anxiety about money.
The most important thing? Pick statements that genuinely resonate with you, and use them with patience and persistence. Over time, these positive words become the gentle soundtrack in your mind—leading your thoughts, feelings, and actions toward greater prosperity.
